Check that a precision matrix solves the graphical lasso

Source: R/glasso.R
glasso_kkt.Rd

glasso_kkt() checks whether a precision matrix solves the graphical lasso for a given correlation or covariance matrix and penalty. The graphical lasso estimates a Gaussian graphical model as the precision (inverse covariance) matrix that maximizes the Gaussian likelihood minus a penalty on the absolute partial associations (Friedman et al., 2008), and a matrix is its solution if and only if it satisfies the optimality (Karush-Kuhn-Tucker) conditions of the problem.

The objective is strictly convex, so it has exactly one optimum, and checking the conditions shows whether a network is the graphical lasso solution without solving the problem a second time. In words, the covariance implied by the precision matrix must equal the observed covariance on the diagonal, differ from it by exactly the penalty for every pair joined by an edge, and by at most the penalty for every pair that is not.

glasso_kkt() returns the largest violation of the conditions; a value near zero shows that the matrix is the optimum, up to numerical precision.

Networks from ebic_glasso() and huge_network() store this value, and certificate() reports it. Unpenalized networks restricted to a graph are checked by ggm_support_kkt(), and nodewise Ising and mixed graphical models by glm_lasso_kkt().

Usage

glasso_kkt(
  theta,
  cor_matrix,
  rho,
  active_tol = 1e-08,
  penalize_diagonal = FALSE
)

Arguments

theta

The precision matrix to check: a finite, square numeric matrix.

cor_matrix

The correlation or covariance matrix the model was fitted to, of the same size as theta.

rho

The penalty: a single finite number >= 0.

active_tol

Absolute value above which an off-diagonal entry of theta counts as an edge. Default 1e-8.

penalize_diagonal

Whether the fit being checked also penalized the diagonal. Default FALSE, the default of ebic_glasso().

Value

A single number, the largest absolute violation of the optimality conditions: 0 at the exact optimum, Inf for an asymmetric or non-positive-definite theta.

Details

The objective, with the penalty on the off-diagonal entries, is $$\min_{\Theta \succ 0} -\log\det\Theta + \mathrm{tr}(S\Theta) + \rho \sum_{i \neq j} |\Theta_{ij}|.$$ With \(W = \Theta^{-1}\), the optimality conditions are \(W_{ii} = S_{ii}\); \(W_{ij} - S_{ij} = \rho\,\mathrm{sign}(\Theta_{ij})\) where \(\Theta_{ij} \neq 0\); and \(|W_{ij} - S_{ij}| \le \rho\) otherwise. The function returns the largest absolute deviation from these conditions. Because the objective is strictly convex, a precision matrix with zero violation is its unique global optimum.

When the penalty also applies to the diagonal (penalize_diagonal = TRUE, the objective adds \(\rho \sum_i |\Theta_{ii}|\)), the diagonal condition becomes \(W_{ii} = S_{ii} + \rho\). Checking a diagonally penalized fit with the default would report a violation of exactly \(\rho\), so this argument must match the fit being checked.

The objective is defined only for symmetric positive-definite matrices, so a theta that is asymmetric (by more than 1e-8) or not positive definite is not a solution and returns Inf.

Conditions

psychnet_bad_input when theta is not a finite square numeric matrix, cor_matrix is not a finite matrix of the same size, rho or active_tol is not a single finite number >= 0, or penalize_diagonal is not TRUE or FALSE.

References

Friedman, J., Hastie, T., & Tibshirani, R. (2008). Sparse inverse covariance estimation with the graphical lasso. Biostatistics, 9(3), 432-441. doi:10.1093/biostatistics/kxm045

See also

certificate(), which reports the stored value of a fitted network; ebic_glasso() and huge_network(); ggm_support_kkt() and glm_lasso_kkt() for the other optimality checks.

Examples

S <- 0.5^abs(outer(1:5, 1:5, "-"))
# At rho = 0 the optimum is the inverse of S, so the violation is ~0 ...
glasso_kkt(solve(S), S, rho = 0)
#> [1] 1.110223e-16
# ... and a perturbed precision matrix violates the conditions.
glasso_kkt(solve(S) + diag(0.1, 5), S, rho = 0)
#> [1] 0.135257
# A fitted network reports the same value through certificate().
certificate(ebic_glasso(cor_matrix = S, n = 200))
#>   method  certificate kind certified
#> 1 glasso 7.168638e-11  kkt      TRUE
